Introductory terminology forms the base for conceptual and theoretical questions in preliminary rounds.

blocks.content: 8. Government Schemes and Current Affairs of Assam
10. Assam GK — Quick Facts and Static GK Compendium

This book covers Assam General Studies in full depth — geography, history, polity, economy, culture, wildlife, personalities, government schemes, and tourism/heritage — built for the Assam Public Service Commission (APSC) and usable across all Assam-based recruitment examinations that include a General Studies or Assam GK component (state police, teaching, clerical, and other state-level exams).

Ten chapters combine detailed conceptual coverage with the exact facts these exams repeatedly test — dates, names, numeric figures, and the Assam-specific institutional details (like the Sixth Schedule autonomous councils) that generic GS material often misses. Every chapter closes with a self-check quiz.

items: Start with Chapters 1–3 (Geography, History, Polity) — these form the factual backbone that later chapters build on.
Chapter 10 is a consolidated quick-facts compendium — use it for final-week revision, not as your first-pass learning material.
Government schemes (Chapter 8) change frequently — treat the figures given as a snapshot and verify against the latest official announcement close to your exam date.
Use the Exam Tip box in every chapter to spot the specific facts and comparisons each exam repeats most often.
Attempt each chapter's quiz without referring back to the notes, then review incorrect answers carefully.

blocks.content: Geography is the single most consistently tested static-GK area across APSC and all Assam recruitment exams — physical features, rivers, and district-level facts recur every cycle.

items: Assam is located in Northeast India, forming the principal gateway to the seven other Northeastern states (often called the 'Seven Sisters', with Assam itself sometimes described as their gateway).

Assam shares international borders with Bhutan (north) and Bangladesh (south), and inter-state borders with Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya, and West Bengal — making it the only Northeastern state bordering the largest number of other states in the region.

The state is connected to the rest of India via the narrow 'Chicken's Neck' (Siliguri Corridor) in West Bengal, a strip of land roughly 20–22 km wide at its narrowest point, making it a geographically and strategically significant land link for the entire Northeast.

Assam is broadly divided into two river valleys — the Brahmaputra Valley (larger, in the north) and the Barak Valley (smaller, in the south) — separated by the Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao hill ranges, which form a distinct upland plateau region between the two valleys.
Total geographical area places Assam among the mid-sized Indian states by area, while its population makes it the most populous state in the entire Northeast region by a considerable margin.

The Brahmaputra is one of the major rivers of Asia, entering Assam from Arunachal Pradesh (where it is known as the Siang/Dihang) and flowing roughly west/southwest across the length of the state before entering Bangladesh.

It is one of the few rivers in the world with a braided channel pattern across much of its course in Assam, and is notable for extensive seasonal flooding that shapes the region's agriculture, settlement patterns, and — significantly — its wildlife ecology, since the annual flood cycle replenishes grasslands critical to parks like Kaziranga.

Majuli, located within the Brahmaputra, is widely cited as one of the world's largest river islands and is a major centre of Assamese neo-Vaishnavite culture (satras); it has faced significant and well-documented erosion over recent decades, a recurring theme in both environmental and current-affairs coverage of the state.

Major tributaries of the Brahmaputra within Assam include the Subansiri, Dhansiri, Manas, Jia Bharali (also called Kameng downstream), and Dibang (joining upstream near the Arunachal border); the Kaziranga-adjacent stretch of the river is particularly significant for its role in shaping the park's grassland ecosystem.

The Brahmaputra is one of very few rivers globally to be legally granted the status of a 'living entity' in certain Indian court rulings aimed at strengthening its environmental protection — a distinctive and occasionally tested current-affairs-adjacent fact.

The Barak River flows through the Barak Valley in southern Assam (comprising the districts of Cachar, Karimganj, and Hailakandi) before entering Bangladesh, where it splits into the Surma and Kushiyara rivers.

The Barak Valley is culturally and linguistically distinct within Assam, with Bengali as the predominant language, in contrast to the Assamese-speaking Brahmaputra Valley — a distinction with real administrative and political significance historically, including past language-policy tensions.
Silchar is the principal town and administrative centre of the Barak Valley, and functions as the region's main commercial and educational hub, home to institutions such as Assam University.

Assam's terrain is predominantly a fertile alluvial plain (the two river valleys), flanked by hill ranges — the Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao (North Cachar Hills) plateau region separates the two valleys and rises noticeably above the surrounding lowlands.

Climate — Assam has a humid subtropical climate with high rainfall, strongly influenced by the southwest monsoon; it receives some of the highest rainfall in India, contributing to the state's characteristic lush vegetation and periodic, sometimes severe, flooding that affects large parts of the Brahmaputra Valley almost every year.

Soil types — mainly alluvial soil in the river valleys (highly fertile, ideal for rice and tea cultivation) and lateritic/hill soil in the upland areas; the state's soil-and-climate combination is a frequently cited explanation for its status as a major tea-producing region.

Seasons — Assam broadly experiences four seasons: a pre-monsoon period (with occasional severe thunderstorms known locally as 'Bordoicila'), the monsoon (June–September, the main rainy season), a post-monsoon/autumn period, and a relatively mild winter.

Assam is divided into multiple administrative divisions and districts, with the number and boundaries of districts having been reorganized periodically — candidates should verify the current official district count and names against the latest state government notification before an exam, since district reorganization has occurred multiple times in recent years and is a frequently updated fact.

Dispur, located within the Guwahati metropolitan area, is the capital of Assam; Guwahati is the largest city and the primary commercial, transportation, and administrative hub of the entire Northeast region.

Guwahati is sometimes referred to as the 'Gateway to the Northeast' given its role as the region's principal transportation, commercial, and administrative hub — it hosts the region's main international airport, is a key railway junction, and serves as headquarters for numerous central government offices covering the whole Northeast.

Each district is headed by a Deputy Commissioner (DC), who holds general administrative, revenue, and (in many contexts) magisterial authority within the district — a structure common across most Indian states but worth knowing precisely for administration-focused GS questions.

cells:
Exam Tip

• The Brahmaputra vs Barak valley distinction (location, language, key districts) is a foundational, guaranteed-to-appear question across nearly every Assam GS paper.

• District names and counts change periodically due to reorganization — always verify the current figure from a recent official source rather than relying on an older number, since this is a frequently updated fact.

• Majuli's status as a major river island and cultural centre is one of the most consistently tested single facts in Assam geography.

blocks.content: Q1. Assam is connected to the rest of India via which narrow land corridor?
Q2. The Barak Valley in southern Assam is predominantly associated with which language?
Q3. Majuli, a major river island, is located in which river?
Q4. Which city is widely referred to as the 'Gateway to the Northeast'?
Q5. Assam shares an international border with which two countries?
